# Federal appeals court clears way for US Army to detonate degraded bomb-making material in Iowa
Published: Nov. 23, 2026 at 12:36 PM CST|Updated: 46 minutes ago
(AP) - A federal appeals court on Monday cleared the way for the U.S. Army to detonate several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, finding that the proposal should adequately limit the dispersal of lead dust into the atmosphere.
In an unusual twist, President Donald Trump, commander in chief of the Army, said on social media earlier in the day that in addition to the court’s go-ahead, he wanted Gov.-elect Rob Sand to approve the detonation. Sand, a Democrat who doesn’t take office until January, has said the decision is fully up to the administration.
A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals said the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust. Those conditions address the concerns of environmental groups that sued to stop the detonation, the court said.

The detonation of 68 barrels of lead azide was initially planned for last Friday, but the Army has since [changed the date](https://apnews.com/article/iowa-army-ammunition-lead-detonation-2d2d7bfaf8ceacddcbea10ed97b097ce) three times following an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects. They had planned for a detonation this coming Wednesday, saying the weather was most favorable that day.

Current Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the state emergency management office on Friday. The state also created a dedicated [website](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fhomelandsecurity.iowa.gov%2Farmy-detonation%3Futm_medium=email%26utm_source=govdelivery/1/010001a205216536-b5cdb25e-af40-4a27-bd9e-cf415420abb6-000000/v93SLPAT5DLgyc2pdYpRoHewbZlrNpK91twu6lKA-K0=452) for information about the operation.
